questions.text: A researcher selected 300 students at random from one school and found that students who studied at least 5 hours a week had higher average scores. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The results can be generalized to all students at the school.
The results can be generalized only to students who volunteered.
Studying causes higher test scores for all students in the city.
No conclusion can be drawn about any group.
questions.explanation: The sample was chosen at random from this school, so the results generalize to the school's students. It was an observational study (no random assignment), so it cannot show causation, and it says nothing about students outside the school.

questions.text: A teacher asked for volunteers to try a new study method. Volunteers who used it scored higher on average than students who did not. Which conclusion is appropriate?
options: Only that the new method is associated with higher scores among volunteers; it cannot be generalized or shown to be the cause.
The new method causes higher scores for all students in the country.
The new method causes higher scores for the volunteers only.
The new method has no effect on scores.
questions.explanation: The students were volunteers (not a random sample), so results cannot be generalized, and they chose the method themselves (no random assignment), so causation cannot be concluded.

questions.text: Researchers randomly selected 200 students from a district and randomly assigned half of them to a tutoring program. The tutored group improved more on average. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Students were randomly assigned, so the program likely caused the improvement for students like those in the study.
The results apply to every school in the world.
Nothing can be concluded because the sample is too large.
The improvement must be due to chance.
questions.explanation: Random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion, and random selection from the district lets the result generalize to students in that district.
